ky_far_side.blurb: A compact sport crag in Coal Bank Hollow, part of the Pendergrass-Murray preserve in the southern Red River Gorge. About a dozen routes, nearly all bolted with a single trad line, run from low 5.10 up through the 5.11s and 5.12s, topping out around 5.13. The wall catches sun early in the day, and a few lines stay climbable when it rains. It works equally well as a short warm-up stop or as the day's main destination if you are projecting sandstone. Expect a modest walk uphill from the lot rather than a roadside crag, and little in the way of crowds.

ky_throwback_crag.blurb: Throwback Crag is a small wall in the Flat Hollow zone of the Red River Gorge, built mostly around bolted face climbing with a pair of trad lines. The mix leans hard: a couple of 5.9s, then a cluster of 5.11s, five or so 5.12s and a few 5.13s. The cliff is slightly overhanging and sees sun early, then stays shaded through most of the day, which suits warm weather but not cold or wet days. It is a good pick when you want to dodge the busier crags nearby. Reach it by a short uphill hike from the road.

ky_dunder_mifflin.blurb: Dunder Mifflin is the main wall of the Office area in the Red River Gorge, a sandstone cliff with about a dozen routes, almost all sport and one easy trad line. One section is a pocketed face under a horizontal roof, and a newer bolted wall adds a good number of moderate lines. The grades start near 5.7 and mostly sit in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, with a single 5.12, so it suits newer leaders as well as those warming up on harder days. A short side crag lies a few minutes further along the cliff to the left.

_expect.name: Land of Boulders (Land of the Arches)

ky_land_of_boulders_land_of_the_arches.blurb: A small cliffline bouldering area in the Red River Gorge, reached from the campground of the same name. Around a dozen sandstone problems are logged, spread over a wide span of heights and difficulty: a few at the easy end (V0 to V2), a cluster of V4s and V5s, and a couple of hard ones in the V6 to V7 range. The rock is good quality and there is plenty of unclimbed potential once more cleaning is done, which makes it a pleasant spot for cool-season outings. A mountain bike trail runs right past the boulders, so watch for riders.

ky_outer_space.blurb: Outer Space is a quiet, shaded sport crag in the Miller Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge, sitting across the hollow from Monster Wall. It holds around a dozen bolted lines on gray sandstone, and the grades skew hard: one route near 5.10, a few 5.12s, a big group at 5.13, and an open 5.15 project. The large overhang on the left can be dirty and would welcome more traffic. Most routes saw little attention for years after being bolted, so expect solitude. The route names follow a space theme. Getting here takes a long, steep walk in on old logging roads.

ky_inner_sanctum.blurb: Inner Sanctum is a sport and trad crag in Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge, set a few hundred feet along the cliff from the neighbouring Sanctuary wall. It holds about a dozen climbs, most of them bolted, with a few crack lines. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.12, and the largest group sits at 5.11, with a handful of easier routes for warming up. It is regarded as a worthwhile stop that is a little less polished than the Sanctuary, and a handy place to tick 5.10 warm-ups before trying harder lines next door. Not the place to go in the rain.

ky_warmup_cluster.blurb: The Warmup Cluster is a trio of boulders at the entrance to the Sun Sector in the Foxtown boulders of eastern Kentucky, with thirteen problems on them. Grades are friendly: mostly V0 to V3 with a few V4s and one V5, so it is ideal for loosening up before moving on to harder boulders deeper in the sector. The walk in drops to a creek and climbs back out, with two boulders on the left of the trail and the third on the right, easy to spot by a long diagonal crack. The boulders mostly face south, so they pick up winter sun in the middle of the day.
